issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify an interface named 'Rideable' with method messageOnRide(), and the template/Main code references Rideable. The solution repository, however, introduces an interface named 'Mountable' (with messageOnRide()) and has an empty Rideable.java file while Pig and Seal implement Mountable. This name/type mismatch between 'Rideable' and 'Mountable' is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which interface to implement and may break tests or expected usage that refer to Rideable.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single interface name consistently. Either rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java (and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable) and remove/replace the empty Rideable.java, or update the problem statement and template to reference Mountable instead of Rideable. Ensure the interface defines messageOnRide() with the expected signature so template, tests, and solution align.

issues.description: The exercise and template refer to an interface named 'Rideable' (UML and Main.java), but the solution implementation uses an interface named 'Mountable' (implemented by Pig and Seal) while leaving Rideable.java empty. This mismatch of the same conceptual interface (animals that can be ridden) across artifacts creates confusion for students mapping the problem description and template code to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the rideable interface across all artifacts. Prefer renaming Mountable (and its file) to Rideable in the solution and update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable, or alternatively change the problem/template references to Mountable—keeping Rideable/Mountable consistent and removing the empty Rideable.java file.
